title: Giraffe snort
author: Anton Baotic, Florian Sicks and Angela S. Stoeger
changes: Giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis) snort, a burst of air through the nostrils; giraffes are nearly silent and the snort is the sound people hear from them most often. Trimmed to 0.10–0.92 s of the original, mixed to mono, gentle 12 dB/oct high-pass at 80 Hz, silence trimmed, loudness-normalised (≈ −18 dBFS RMS, peak ≤ −1 dBFS), peaks limited by 2.0 dB, 10 ms fade-in / 120 ms fade-out, encoded as 96 kbps mono MP3. The high-pass is set to 80 Hz because the original has strong rumble below 80 Hz that is just as loud before and after the snort; the snort itself is above 100 Hz.
